hints.content:
$g$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by zero point five. The graph of y equals g of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative four point seven-five, negative one and it increases through the x-intercept negative three, zero. It continues to increase until the local maximum at negative one point five, one. Then it decreases to a local minimum at the origin. Then it increases to a local maximum at one point five, one. Then it decreases through the x-intercept three, zero and the point four point seven-five, negative one. The function is highlighted from x equals negative four point seven-five to x equals negative one point five and from x equals zero to one point five.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4<x<-3$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-2.5<x<-2$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$0.5<x<1.5$ |  $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
